### 2.1 Quantum Numbers & Electronic Configuration (Quantum Numbers)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **218 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Orbital shapes, quantum numbers $(n, l, m_l, m_s)$, nodal surfaces, and anomalous configurations ($\text{Cr}: 3d^5 4s^1, \text{Cu}: 3d^{10} 4s^1$).

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Radial nodes} = n - l - 1, \quad \text{Angular nodes} = l, \quad \text{Total nodes} = n - 1, \quad \mu_s = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM}$ depends on $n$, which is the number of UNPAIRED electrons, not total electrons!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Degeneracy of hydrogen atom at energy level $n$ is $n^2$ (without spin) or $2n^2$ (including spin).

- **[2026 Morning Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"Which of the following is correct set of 4 quantum numbers of $19^{\text{th}}$ electron in Chromium (Atomic number $=24$ ) in accordance wit..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Bohr's Orbitals & Electronic Transitions (Bohr Model)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **35 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Electronic energy levels in hydrogenic species, wave number $\bar{\nu}$, and emission spectral series.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
r_n = 0.529 \frac{n^2}{Z}\text{ \AA}, \quad E_n = -13.6 \frac{Z^2}{n^2}\text{ eV}, \quad \bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^2\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Rydberg formula requires multiplication by $Z^2$ for single-electron ions like $\text{He}^+$ ($Z=2$) and $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ($Z=3$).

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Limiting line (series limit) of any spectral series occurs when $n_2 = \infty \implies \bar{\nu}_{\text{limit}} = \frac{R Z^2}{n_1^2}$.

#### Linked Representative PYQs:

- **[2026 Morning Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"If shortest wavelength of hydrogen atom in Lyman series is $x$ , then longest wavelength in Balmer series of $He^{+}$ is:..."* — **Correct Answer: A**
- **[2026 Evening Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"The wavelength of spectral line obtained in the spectrum of $Li^{2+}$ ion, when the transition takes place between two levels whose sum is 4..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.3 Heisenberg Uncertainty & De Broglie Wavelength (Wave Mechanics)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **18 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Limits of simultaneous precision in position and momentum, and dual wave nature of micro-particles.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi} = \frac{\hbar}{2}, \quad \Delta x \cdot m\Delta v \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}, \quad \lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: If uncertainty in position and momentum are equal ($\Delta x = \Delta p$), then $\Delta v = \frac{1}{2m}\sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}}$.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: De Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through potential $V$ volts: $\lambda \approx \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\text{ \AA}$.

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring JEE Mains Pitfalls in Structure of Atom Syllabus reduced

### 1. Sign Convention & Vector Inversion Errors
Paper-setters frequently exploit sign confusion in energy and potential differences. Always write the fundamental thermodynamic / vector definition before substituting numerical values.

### 2. Unit System Discrepancies
Molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), SI vs CGS units, and micro/milli/nano multipliers (10^-3, 10^-6, 10^-9) account for over 35% of calculation mistakes in numerical type questions.

### 3. Boundary & Extreme Conditions
In transient circuits or limiting conditions (t=0+, t -> inf, infinite dilution, resonance), always check the asymptotic behavior of inductors, capacitors, and electrolyte mobility.

### 4. Direct Addition Fallacy
Never algebraically add intensive quantities (such as electrode potentials or AC component voltages) without accounting for electron weighting (n1*E1 + n2*E2 = n3*E3) or phasor vector geometry (V_total = sqrt(V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2)).
